summary: This article presents an overview of key scientific challenges in the astrophysics and astrochemistry of the interstellar and intergalactic media. Addressing many of these challenges will become possible with the Russian space observatory Spektr-UF, which is currently being prepared for launch. The ultraviolet (UV) spectral range is critically important for studying the evolution of the Universe, as it contains fundamental absorption and emission lines of most chemical elements and the most important molecules. These lines make it possible to reliably determine the physical conditions and chemical composition of various astrophysical objects, as well as the characteristics of the processes occurring within them. The article examines the prospects for UV observations across a broad range of scientific problems, from investigating the epoch of helium reionization and the thermal history of the Universe to mapping ongoing star formation in galaxies. Dedicated sections address the study of the chemical evolution of galaxies at intermediate redshifts, the distribution of "hidden" baryons and metals, the small-scale structure of interstellar clouds, the physics of photodissociation regions and protoplanetary disks, and the modeling of UV emission from nebulae surrounding fast-moving pulsars. The high sensitivity and spectral resolution of the Spektr-UF instruments are expected to provide fundamentally new data across all these research areas, filling existing gaps in our understanding of the interstellar and intergalactic media.

AI.tldr: Overview of key astrophysical/astrochemical challenges in the interstellar and intergalactic media and how the upcoming Russian UV observatory Spektr-UF can address them through high-sensitivity, high-resolution ultraviolet spectroscopy.
AI.motivation: The UV band hosts fundamental absorption/emission lines of most elements and key molecules, enabling reliable determination of physical conditions and chemical composition; however, existing gaps remain in understanding the interstellar and intergalactic media, and current facilities lack adequate UV sensitivity and resolution.
AI.method: Review/organizational strategy: identify major open problems and map them onto the capabilities of Spektr-UF's UV instrumentation, with dedicated sections on specific science cases (He reionization epoch, thermal history, star-formation mapping, chemical evolution at intermediate redshift, hidden baryons/metals, small-scale cloud structure, PDR and protoplanetary-disk physics, pulsar-wind nebula emission modeling).
AI.result: The paper frames the science potential of Spektr-UF: its high sensitivity and spectral resolution are anticipated to deliver fundamentally new UV data across all enumerated research areas, filling existing gaps in understanding the interstellar and intergalactic media.
AI.conclusion: Spektr-UF, currently being prepared for launch, offers broad prospects for UV observations spanning helium-reionization studies to galaxy star-formation mapping, and is expected to substantially advance the astrophysics and astrochemistry of the interstellar and intergalactic media.

title: The Galah survey and symbiotic stars. II. Discovery, validation, and intensive follow-up of 44 new systems accreting at the lowest detectable levels
summary: We report the discovery, validation, and characterization of 44 new symbiotic stars (SySts) accreting at the lowest detectable levels (Lacc =< 3 Lsun). Candidates were initially selected from the Galah survey among non-pulsating M-type red giants exhibiting Halpha excess. Between 2021 and 2025, these targets were subjected to intensive multi-wavelength campaigns, including ground-based, high-resolution Echelle spectroscopy over 544 nights, multi-epoch flickering searches down to 1 mmag, and UV/X-ray observations with the Swift satellite. Our high-resolution spectra allowed for a detailed investigation of Halpha flux and line-profile variability. Crucially, the radial velocities measured for the M-giant components yielded reliable spectroscopic orbits for 22 objects and preliminary orbits for an additional eight, corroborated by binary-induced modulations in ASAS-SN photometry. Measured accretion levels vary by factors of up to 20X, emphasizing the need for high-sensitivity, long-term monitoring. Swift X-ray data exclude neutron star companions in all targets, consistent with predominance of white-dwarf degenerates in known SySts. Combined with the 33 objects from Paper I, this sample of 77 new SySts significantly exceeds the number of previously known, accreting-only Galactic symbiotic stars, constituting the bulk of the low-accretion (LowAcc) variety discovered to date and representing >10 percent of all known SySts in the Galaxy. As SySts likely spend most of their lifetimes in LowAcc faint states, characterizing this population is essential for estimating the total Galactic SySt population and evaluating the role of SySts as Type Ia supernova progenitors or sources of UV excess in elliptical galaxies.

AI.tldr: The paper reports the discovery, validation, and characterization of 44 new low-accretion symbiotic stars from the Galah survey, expanding the known Galactic population and establishing the LowAcc variety as a dominant component.
AI.motivation: Symbiotic stars likely spend most of their lifetimes in faint, low-accretion states, so characterizing this population is essential for estimating the total Galactic SySt population and assessing their role as Type Ia supernova progenitors or sources of UV excess in elliptical galaxies.
AI.method: Candidates were selected from the Galah survey among non-pulsating M-type red giants showing Halpha excess. From 2021–2025 they were observed with high-resolution Echelle spectroscopy over 544 nights, multi-epoch flickering searches down to 1 mmag, and Swift UV/X-ray observations, complemented by ASAS-SN photometry for binary modulations and radial-velocity orbit fitting.
AI.result: 44 new SySts were confirmed at accretion levels Lacc =< 3 Lsun. Reliable spectroscopic orbits were derived for 22 objects and preliminary orbits for 8 more, corroborated by ASAS-SN photometric modulations. Halpha flux and line-profile variability were characterized, accretion levels vary by up to 20x, and Swift X-ray data exclude neutron-star companions in all targets, consistent with white-dwarf predominance. Together with 33 objects from Paper I, the 77 new SySts exceed the previously known accreting-only Galactic population and represent >10% of all known Galactic SySts.
AI.conclusion: The sample constitutes the bulk of the low-accretion SySt variety discovered to date, highlighting the need for high-sensitivity long-term monitoring and providing a critical basis for population estimates and for evaluating SySts as Type Ia supernova progenitors or UV-excess sources in elliptical galaxies.

title: Mass-Metallicity Relation of the Fossil Disk in Six Nearby Galaxies using JWST RGB Stars
comment: Accepted for publication in ApJL. 10 pages, 4 figures and 1 table
summary: We here present the first ever mass-metallicity relation (MZR) of fossil disk populations using the resolved stellar populations in the James Webb Space Telescope Near-Infrared Camera (JWST/NIRCam) images of six nearby galaxies. Both the mass and metallicity were determined using the Red Giant Branch (RGB) stars, employing methods that have been well established to study the halo populations of nearby galaxies using the Hubble Space Telescope images. Specifically, we obtained the mass and metallicity by comparing the color, magnitude and number density near the tip of the RGB (TRGB) stars in the F115W$-$F200W vs F200W color-magnitude diagrams (CMDs) with that of the PARSEC isochrones of 4 and 13~Gyr. The RGB metallicities of the disks of nearby galaxies closely match those found in galaxies at redshifts $z>8$, with the metallicity range following a power-law relation with the fossil disk mass. The power-law index of the fossil disk MZR, $γ\approx0.26$, compares well with the typical value found in MZRs obtained using gas metallicities across redshifts. Through this work, we illustrate the utility of JWST/NIRCam images for obtaining the mass and metallicity of the fossil disks of nearby galaxies at precisions that were not possible earlier, which opens up a new method to carry out the near-field cosmological studies.

AI.tldr: The paper presents the first mass-metallicity relation (MZR) for fossil disk populations of six nearby galaxies, derived from resolved RGB stars in JWST/NIRCam imaging, finding a power-law index γ≈0.26 consistent with gas-based MZRs across redshifts.
AI.motivation: To establish a near-field cosmological method for studying fossil disk populations and to connect the metallicities of nearby galaxy disks with those of high-redshift (z>8) galaxies, which previously lacked a direct, high-precision comparison using resolved stellar populations.
AI.method: Mass and metallicity were determined from Red Giant Branch (RGB) stars in six nearby galaxies using JWST/NIRCam F115W−F200W vs F200W color-magnitude diagrams. The color, magnitude, and number density near the tip of the RGB (TRGB) were compared with PARSEC isochrones at 4 and 13 Gyr, building on methods established for HST studies of halo populations.
AI.result: The RGB metallicities of the disks closely match those of galaxies at z>8. The metallicity follows a power-law relation with fossil disk mass, with index γ≈0.26, in good agreement with typical values from gas-metallicity MZRs across redshifts.
AI.conclusion: JWST/NIRCam imaging enables mass and metallicity measurements of fossil disks in nearby galaxies at unprecedented precision, offering a new avenue for near-field cosmological studies and linking local disk populations to high-redshift galaxy properties.

title: Metamorphic novae. I. Gaia22alz -- Violent relaxation starting from static evolution
comment: 17 pages, 9 figures, accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: Gaia22alz (nova Vel 2022) shows characteristic properties in its light curves and spectral evolution similar to slow novae HR Del, V723 Cas, and V5558 Sgr. Their outburst begins in a way of hydrostatic expansion with no mass loss, followed by large amplitude ($ΔV \sim 2$ mag) multiple peaks around the mean magnitude of $M_V \sim -5.5$, and eventually it decays similarly to normal classical novae. We present a light curve model of Gaia22alz based on our metamorphic nova theory: a nova starts from a static expansion and then metamorphoses to an optically thick wind evolution through a large amplitude multiple peak phase as a violent relaxation process. Our theoretical light curve for the rising phase consistently explains the slow rise and early spectral evolution of Gaia22alz. Gaia22als is a close binary as well as other three novae, which is consistent with our metamorphic nova theory that the companion motion in the nova envelope triggers the metamorphic transition. Our results do not support E. Aydi et al.'s explanation that the slow optical rise of Gaia22alz is owing to the irradiation of X-ray/UV flash.

AI.tldr: A metamorphic nova model reproduces the slow rise and spectral evolution of Gaia22alz, whose light curve and spectral development resemble those of slow novae HR Del, V723 Cas, and V5558 Sgr, supporting a hydrostatic-expansion-then-stellar-wind transition triggered by companion motion rather than X-ray/UV irradiation.
AI.motivation: Gaia22alz (nova Vel 2022) exhibits light-curve and spectral-evolution characteristics similar to slow novae HR Del, V723 Cas, and V5558 Sgr: onset via hydrostatic expansion without mass loss, large-amplitude (ΔV ~ 2 mag) multiple peaks near M_V ~ -5.5, and eventual decay like classical novae. The authors aim to explain the rising phase and test competing interpretations of the slow optical rise, in particular the irradiation-of-X-ray/UV-flash scenario proposed by Aydi et al.
AI.method: The authors construct a light-curve model of Gaia22alz within their metamorphic nova theory, in which a nova begins with a static (hydrostatic) expansion and then 'metamorphoses' into an optically thick wind phase, passing through a large-amplitude multiple-peak phase as a violent relaxation process. The theoretical light curve for the rising phase is computed and compared with the observed slow rise and early spectral evolution. The binary nature (close companion) of Gaia22alz and the three comparison novae is also examined as the physical trigger of the metamorphic transition.
AI.result: The theoretical rising-phase light curve consistently accounts for the slow rise and early spectral evolution of Gaia22alz. Gaia22alz is confirmed to be a close binary, as are the other three slow novae, in line with the prediction that companion motion within the nova envelope triggers the metamorphic transition. The results do not support Aydi et al.'s explanation that the slow optical rise is due to irradiation by the X-ray/UV flash.
AI.conclusion: The metamorphic nova theory provides a coherent account of Gaia22alz's slow rise, multiple-peak behavior, and spectral evolution, with the binary companion's motion acting as the trigger for the transition from hydrostatic expansion to optically thick wind. The irradiation-based interpretation of the slow optical rise is disfavored.

title: An automated photometric pipeline for measuring the corotation radius of spiral galaxies
summary: The corotation radius R_CR of a spiral galaxy marks the radius where the angular speed of the spiral pattern matches the orbital speed of the disk material. Despite its importance for understanding spiral structure and galaxy evolution, very few galaxies have corotation measurements, often derived using heterogeneous techniques. We present an automated photometric pipeline that identifies corotation radii by tracking the azimuthal phase offset between young and old stellar populations. Building on the color-gradient framework of \citet{Puerari1997}, we extract azimuthal brightness profiles from deprojected dual-band images, fit periodic models to the profiles, and identify corotation candidates at radii where the phase difference between the two stellar tracers changes sign. Each candidate is assigned an adaptive uncertainty interval and reported with a goodness-of-fit metric. We benchmark the method against a cross-method literature compilation, scoring every technique -- including our own -- against a reference built from the published measurements alone and evaluated leave-one-out. Over the $90$ galaxies for which such a reference exists, the pipeline places a correct corotation radius in $80.0\%$ of them, recovers $63.6\%$ of their known corotation radii, and reaches a harmonic mean of recall and purity of $0.58$, the highest values of any method in the comparison. Unlike the published methods, each of which was applied to a small, curated set of galaxies, our pipeline is run on the entire reference sample without any pre-selection, a sample two to six times larger than existing methods. The pipeline is scalable to large surveys, flexible with respect to spiral mode, and naturally recovers multiple corotation radii in galaxies with complex spiral structure, providing a uniform framework for studying disk resonances across diverse galaxy populations.

AI.tldr: An automated photometric pipeline measures spiral galaxy corotation radii by tracking the sign flip of the azimuthal phase offset between young and old stellar populations in deprojected dual-band images; benchmarked against a literature compilation, it outperforms published methods while running without pre-selection on a larger sample.
AI.motivation: Corotation radii are central to understanding spiral structure and disk evolution, yet very few galaxies have such measurements, and those available come from heterogeneous techniques applied to small, curated samples. A uniform, scalable method is needed.
AI.method: Building on the color-gradient framework of Puerari (1997), the pipeline extracts azimuthal brightness profiles from deprojected dual-band images, fits periodic models to them, and flags corotation candidates at radii where the phase difference between young and old stellar tracers changes sign. Each candidate gets an adaptive uncertainty interval and a goodness-of-fit metric. Evaluation uses a leave-one-out reference built from published measurements only, across 90 galaxies.
AI.result: The pipeline places a correct corotation radius in 80.0% of galaxies, recovers 63.6% of known corotation radii, and achieves a harmonic mean of recall and purity of 0.58 — the highest of any method compared — applied with no pre-selection to a sample two to six times larger than existing methods.
AI.conclusion: The method is scalable to large surveys, flexible with respect to spiral mode, and naturally recovers multiple corotation radii in galaxies with complex spiral structure, offering a uniform framework for studying disk resonances across diverse galaxy populations.

title: The vertical distribution of molecular gas in the fourth quadrant of the Milky Way
comment: 6 pages + 6 pages appendices, accepted for publication in A&A
summary: The vertical distribution of molecular gas in the Milky Way disk is poorly studied, especially in the 4th quadrant and the far side of the Galaxy. While surveys over 20 years ago suffered from coarse beam and non-Nyquist sampling, most of the recent surveys are limited to $|b|<1^\circ$ and/or focus on the Northern Galactic plane. We examine the molecular gas's vertical distribution and properties in the fourth quadrant to check the impact of Galactic structure on current star formation. We mapped two arm tangent regions ($l=[329^\circ.0,327^\circ.0]$ for the Norma-Outer arm, and $l=[310^\circ.0,308^\circ.5]$ for the Scutum-Centaurus arm) with the $^{12}$CO 3-2 line using the 7-pixel LASMA receiver of the APEX 12 m telescope, covering up to $b=[-2^\circ,+2^\circ]$ (or $|z|\sim200$ pc near the tangent points). The noise level of the $^{12}$CO 3-2 line is about 0.4 K [$T_{MB}$] in velocity channels of 0.5 km s$^{-1}$. The vertical distribution around the tangent regions of the spiral arm is fitted with two Gaussian components, the narrow one with an FWHM thickness of 25 pc and the wide one of about 100 pc. Two explanations are proposed: they are two sub-components of the thin disk (the narrowest tracing the spiral arm and the other the inter arms components), or they trace both thin and thick disks that show a smaller thickness when observed with CO 3-2 than when observed with CO 1-0. The latter indicates that the density distribution of the interstellar medium exhibits a steeper gradient at larger heights above the plane. Clumps in the two tangent regions are searched and divided into groups by relative height. Compared with the low relative height clumps ($|z|<50$ pc), the median relative height clumps ($50~\mathrm{pc}<|z|<100~\mathrm{pc}$) have lower excitation temperature and surface density, with fewer high values in the distribution. A similar tentative trend is found for the mass.

AI.tldr: We mapped two spiral-arm tangent regions in the fourth Galactic quadrant with APEX $^{12}$CO 3-2 out to $|z|\sim200$ pc, finding the vertical gas distribution is well fit by two Gaussians (FWHM ≈25 pc and ≈100 pc).
AI.motivation: The vertical distribution of molecular gas in the Galactic disk is poorly constrained, especially in the 4th quadrant and on the far side. Older surveys had coarse beams and non-Nyquist sampling, while most recent surveys are limited to $|b|<1^\circ$ and/or the Northern Galactic plane, leaving the impact of Galactic structure on present-day star formation unclear.
AI.method: Using the 7-pixel LASMA receiver on the APEX 12 m telescope, the authors mapped two arm tangent regions ($l=329^\circ.0$–$327^\circ.0$, Norma-Outer arm; $l=310^\circ.0$–$308^\circ.5$, Scutum-Centaurus arm) in $^{12}$CO 3-2, covering $b=[-2^\circ,+2^\circ]$ (|z|∼200 pc) with a noise of ~0.4 K [$T_{MB}$] at 0.5 km s$^{-1}$ channels. The vertical distribution was fit with two Gaussian components, and clumps were identified and grouped by relative height $|z|$.
AI.result: The vertical distribution near the arm tangent regions is described by a narrow component (FWHM ≈25 pc) and a wide component (FWHM ≈100 pc). Relative-height clump comparison shows that median-height clumps ($50<|z|<100$ pc) have lower excitation temperature and surface density than low-height clumps ($|z|<50$ pc), with fewer high-value outliers; mass shows a similar tentative trend.
AI.conclusion: The two components are interpreted either as two sub-components of the thin disk (narrow traces the spiral arm, wide the inter-arm gas) or as thin plus thick disk, with the latter implying a steeper density gradient of the interstellar medium at larger heights (CO 3-2 yields a thinner apparent disk than CO 1-0). Gas properties degrade with height above the plane, consistent with structured, arm-dominated molecular gas in the fourth quadrant.

title: Tidal Evolution of Satellite Dwarf Galaxies. I. Tidal Tracks of Stellar Mass and Structure
comment: Submitted to ApJ. Paper II is coming soon
summary: Satellite dwarf galaxies are reshaped by the tidal field of their host, a process that may account for part of the structural diversity of the observed dwarf population. We study how the stellar component of a satellite responds to tidal stripping using a suite of 480 controlled $N$-body simulations of satellite galaxies consisting of both dark matter (DM) and stars orbiting a Milky-Way-mass host. The simulated dwarfs span a broad range of DM halo structural and stellar-distribution parameters, including halo concentration, inner density slope, stellar-to-halo mass ratio, compactness of the stellar distribution with respect to the halo, as well as the Sérsic index of the stellar profiles. We present a comprehensive library of tidal tracks, namely, the evolution of the stellar mass, half-mass radius, mean surface density, and line-of-sight velocity dispersion, as functions of the bound mass fraction of the hosting DM subhalo, and provide simple and accurate fitting functions. We also identify the dependence of tidal tracks on key factors in the initial structural conditions. Notably, stellar compactness determines the duration over which the stellar mass remains relatively intact while the surrounding DM is being stripped. The Sérsic index and inner DM slope, in turn, govern the late-stage stellar mass-loss slope and the contraction or expansion of the remnant. Our simulations and empirical models provide a framework for modelling the stellar evolution of satellites across a broad range of progenitor structures, useful for semi-analytical models of satellite galaxy evolution.

AI.tldr: 480 controlled N-body simulations reveal how tidal stripping reshapes satellite dwarf galaxies' stellar components, yielding a library of tidal tracks fit with simple functions and identifying which initial structural parameters control stellar mass loss, size evolution, and velocity dispersion.
AI.motivation: Satellite dwarf galaxies are reshaped by their host's tidal field, which may explain part of the structural diversity of observed dwarfs. The paper aims to characterize how the stellar component of a satellite responds to tidal stripping across a broad range of progenitor structures.
AI.method: A suite of 480 controlled N-body simulations of satellites with both dark matter (DM) and stars orbiting a Milky-Way-mass host. Simulated dwarfs span wide ranges in DM halo concentration, inner density slope, stellar-to-halo mass ratio, stellar compactness relative to the halo, and Sérsic index of stellar profiles.
AI.result: A comprehensive library of tidal tracks—evolution of stellar mass, half-mass radius, mean surface density, and line-of-sight velocity dispersion as functions of the bound DM subhalo mass fraction—with simple, accurate fitting functions. Stellar compactness sets how long stellar mass remains intact while DM is stripped; Sérsic index and inner DM slope govern the late-stage stellar mass-loss slope and remnant contraction or expansion.
AI.conclusion: Tidal tracks depend systematically on initial structural conditions. The simulations and empirical models provide a framework for modeling satellite stellar evolution across a broad range of progenitor structures, useful for semi-analytical models of satellite galaxy evolution.

title: Constraining Dust Properties Along the Minor Axis of Andromeda
comment: 15 pages, 12 figures. Accepted for publication in A&A
summary: Previous studies of dust emission in M31 based primarily on Herschel data have reported inconsistent radial trends in the dust emissivity index ($β$), partly due to limited wavelength coverage and the intrinsic $T_{\rm dust}$-$β$ degeneracy. We aim to improve the constraints of $β$ determinations and obtain the spatial surface density and temperature distributions at GMC scales in M31 by extending the spectral coverage into the millimeter regime and by quantifying the impact of wavelength coverage on the $T_{\rm dust}$-$β$ degeneracy. We present new IRAM 30m NIKA2 1.15 mm observations along the minor axis of M31 at an angular resolution of 11 arcsec, corresponding to $\sim 40$ pc at the distance of M31. These data are used with Herschel and JCMT SCUBA-2 maps to perform pixel-by-pixel single-component modified blackbody fitting. Including the 850 $μ$m and 1.15 mm data helps reduce the $T_{\rm dust}$-$β$ degeneracy and yields an average emissivity index of $β\approx 1.8$, systematically lower than values derived from far-infrared-only analyses. Radial analysis shows higher $β$ values in the 5 kpc ring compared to the 10 kpc ring. The elevated $β$ values in the inner 5 kpc may be linked to changes in dust composition, potentially associated with enhanced starlight heating in this region. Millimeter wavelength coverage is important for improving $β$ constraints in M31. The lower $β$ values inferred from the 250--1150 $μ$m SED fitting suggest possible variations in dust emissivity and highlight the importance of sampling the long-wavelength SED slope in nearby galaxies.

AI.tldr: New IRAM 30m NIKA2 1.15 mm observations of M31, combined with Herschel and SCUBA-2 data, reduce the T–β degeneracy and yield an average dust emissivity index β ≈ 1.8, systematically lower than far-infrared-only estimates, with higher β in the 5 kpc ring than the 10 kpc ring.
AI.motivation: Previous M31 dust-emission studies, based mainly on Herschel data, reported inconsistent radial trends in the dust emissivity index β, partly because of limited wavelength coverage and the intrinsic T_dust–β degeneracy. The authors aim to tighten β constraints and map the dust surface density and temperature at GMC scales, and to quantify how wavelength coverage affects the degeneracy.
AI.method: Pixel-by-pixel single-component modified blackbody fitting to new IRAM 30m NIKA2 1.15 mm observations along M31's minor axis (11 arcsec, ~40 pc resolution), combined with Herschel and JCMT SCUBA-2 maps extending coverage to 850 μm and 1.15 mm.
AI.result: Adding the 850 μm and 1.15 mm data reduces the T_dust–β degeneracy and gives an average β ≈ 1.8, systematically lower than far-infrared-only values. Radial analysis shows higher β in the 5 kpc ring than in the 10 kpc ring; the elevated inner β may reflect changes in dust composition, possibly linked to enhanced starlight heating.
AI.conclusion: Millimeter wavelength coverage is important for improving β constraints in M31. The lower β from 250–1150 μm SED fitting suggests possible variations in dust emissivity and highlights the importance of sampling the long-wavelength SED slope in nearby galaxies.

title: HI Emission Recovery in the Low-Redshift Radio Population: Host-Galaxy and Radio-Luminosity Dependence in FASHI and LoTSS
comment: 25 pages,6 figures, submitted to ApJ
summary: Overlapping blind 21 cm and wide-area low-frequency continuum surveys make it possible to measure which radio sources an untargeted HI survey recovers. Cross-matching FASHI DR1 with the LoTSS DR2 value-added catalog yields 4392 one-to-one associations. Within an empirically defined comparison region of $2912$\,deg$^2$, we construct a low-redshift, spectroscopic, radio-selected parent of 25,573 LoTSS sources whose expected HI line falls in the FASHI band, and measure how often each is recovered. Sources classified as radio-loud AGN in the published LoTSS DR2 radio-AGN classification are recovered less often than star-forming ones: 143 of 1542 ($9.27\%$, $7.87$--$10.83$) against $14.88\%$ ($14.43$--$15.33$) of 24,031, an odds ratio of $0.585$ ($0.491$--$0.697$). The two classes, however, differ strongly in host properties, by $1.34$ dex in median specific star formation rate, and within their overlapping stellar-mass and star-formation ranges we detect no statistically significant residual class difference (adjusted odds ratio $1.60$, $0.87$--$2.94$). In contrast, 144 MHz luminosity remains positively associated with HI recovery after adjustment for the measured host properties, redshift and an approximate sensitivity proxy: within the same overlapping range, each dex raises the odds of recovery by a factor of $2.03$ ($1.54$--$2.68$), an association carried primarily by the star-forming population, not by the radio-AGN subsample. We interpret this as an empirical relationship with detectable HI emission, not as evidence that radio activity increases or decreases HI mass. The association catalog and the controlled recovery measurements characterize the radio population sampled by a blind HI survey.

AI.tldr: Cross-matching FASHI DR1 with LoTSS DR2, this study measures which radio sources a blind HI survey recovers, finding that radio-loud AGN are recovered less often than star-forming galaxies, but the difference vanishes after controlling for host properties, while 144 MHz luminosity remains positively associated with HI recovery.
AI.motivation: To characterize the radio population sampled by an untargeted blind HI survey, the authors need to know which types of radio sources such a survey actually recovers and why.
AI.method: Cross-match FASHI DR1 with the LoTSS DR2 value-added catalog (4392 one-to-one associations), build a low-redshift spectroscopic radio-selected parent of 25,573 LoTSS sources within a 2912 deg^2 comparison region whose expected HI line falls in the FASHI band, and measure per-source recovery rates; compare radio-loud AGN vs star-forming classes and apply adjustments for host properties (sSFR, stellar mass), redshift and an approximate sensitivity proxy.
AI.result: Radio-loud AGN are recovered less often than star-forming sources (9.27%, 143/1542, vs 14.88%, 14.43-15.33% of 24,031; odds ratio 0.585, 0.491-0.697). The classes differ by 1.34 dex in median sSFR, and within their overlapping stellar-mass and star-formation ranges no significant residual class difference remains (adjusted odds ratio 1.60, 0.87-2.94). In contrast, 144 MHz luminosity remains positively associated with HI recovery after adjustment: each dex raises recovery odds by 2.03 (1.54-2.68), driven mainly by the star-forming population.
AI.conclusion: The apparent radio-AGN deficit in HI recovery is attributable to host-galaxy properties rather than radio activity; the positive luminosity association is an empirical link to detectable HI emission, not evidence that radio activity changes HI mass. The catalog and controlled recovery measurements characterize the radio population sampled by a blind HI survey.

title: Probing the Faint Outskirts of Star-Forming Galaxies with 1<z<9 Using Stacked Images
comment: 19 pages, 15 figures, accepted for publication in ApJL
summary: We present a systematic study of the faint outer light profiles of star-forming galaxies using deep JWST/NIRCam imaging from the CEERS, JADES, and PRIMER surveys. Our sample consists of 14,812 face-on disk galaxies at $1<z<9$ with $\log(M_*/M_{\odot})>8.5$, selected from the DAWN JWST Archive. To characterize the low-surface-brightness outskirts beyond the effective radius ($R_e$), we stack galaxies in bins of stellar mass and redshift, accounting for cosmological surface-brightness dimming, angular-size scaling, and PSF convolution, and estimate residual backgrounds from blank-sky stacks. The color profiles generally become bluer toward larger radii, indicating negative color gradients and supporting an inside-out growth scenario. Galaxies with $\log(M_*/M_{\odot}) < 9.5$ at $z>2.5$ exhibit a weak reversal in their outermost regions, suggesting more complex stellar population gradients at early times. The outer light profiles generally exhibit a good exponential decline with radius, and the outer scale lengths measured beyond $2R_e$ show mass and redshift dependences remarkably similar to those of the conventional mass-size relation. This similarity suggests that the extended outer light is closely linked to the same processes governing the growth of the inner galaxy, rather than providing a direct tracer of ex-situ stellar components in the early universe. We also find little wavelength dependence in the outer scale lengths, indicating that dust attenuation likely has a limited impact at these radii. These results provide new constraints on the buildup of extended stellar distributions during cosmic noon and at earlier epochs.

AI.tldr: Deep JWST/NIRCam stacking of 14,812 face-on disk galaxies at 1<z<9 reveals bluer-outward color profiles (inside-out growth) and outer exponential scale lengths whose mass–redshift dependence mirrors the mass–size relation, suggesting the extended outer light traces inner-galaxy growth rather than dominant ex-situ components.
AI.motivation: The low-surface-brightness outskirts of high-redshift star-forming galaxies are poorly constrained, yet they encode how stellar mass assembled over cosmic time (inside-out growth vs. ex-situ accretion). The authors aim to characterize these faint outer profiles systematically across a wide mass and redshift range to test whether extended light traces in-situ growth or external channels.
AI.method: Sample of 14,812 face-on disk galaxies at 1<z<9 with log(M*/Msun)>8.5 from the DAWN JWST Archive, using deep JWST/NIRCam imaging from CEERS, JADES, and PRIMER. Galaxies are stacked in bins of stellar mass and redshift beyond R_e; the analysis corrects for cosmological surface-brightness dimming, angular-size scaling, and PSF convolution, and residual backgrounds are estimated from blank-sky stacks. Color profiles, exponential outer scale lengths beyond 2R_e, and their wavelength dependence are measured.
AI.result: Color profiles generally become bluer with radius (negative color gradients), supporting inside-out growth; galaxies with log(M*/Msun)<9.5 at z>2.5 show a weak reversal in the outermost regions, indicating more complex stellar-population gradients at early times. Outer light declines approximately exponentially, and outer scale lengths beyond 2R_e follow mass and redshift trends remarkably similar to the conventional mass–size relation. Little wavelength dependence is found in outer scale lengths, implying limited dust impact at these radii.
AI.conclusion: The extended outer light is closely linked to the same processes governing inner-galaxy growth rather than being a direct tracer of ex-situ stellar components in the early universe. Dust attenuation has limited effect in the outskirts, and these results place new constraints on the buildup of extended stellar distributions at cosmic noon and earlier epochs.

title: The TNG50-SKIRT Atlas: Multi-wavelength properties of galaxy discs in the TNG50 simulation
comment: 14 pages, 9 figures, accepted
summary: We investigate the wavelength dependence of disc scale lengths in galaxies from the TNG50-SKIRT Atlas (TSA), and assess whether the simulated galaxies reproduce the structural properties and scaling relations observed in real galaxies. We measure disc scale lengths from 1D radial surface-brightness profiles of multi-wavelength synthetic images. The disc-dominated region is defined interactively per galaxy and applied consistently across bands. We restrict the analysis to nearly face-on, star-forming galaxies and retain only systems whose r-band profiles are well described by an exponential model. The resulting scale lengths are compared to observational samples and analysed using both dust-attenuated and dust-free images, as well as intrinsic stellar population maps. We find that the majority of TSA galaxies exhibit exponential discs in realistic mock observations. TSA galaxies reproduce the observed disc scale length-stellar mass (luminosity) relation, but are systematically larger at fixed mass or luminosity. The dependence of disc scale length on morphology is weak. Disc scale lengths correlate strongly across wavelengths, but decrease systematically with increasing wavelength. When normalised by the stellar-mass scale length, TSA galaxies exhibit a monotonic trend consistent with observations over the optical-to-NIR range. Comparing dust-free and dust-attenuated images and linking the results to intrinsic galaxy properties, we find that stellar population gradients are the primary driver of this wavelength dependence. In particular, radial gradients in stellar age dominate the effect, while metallicity gradients play a secondary role. Dust attenuation further enhances the wavelength dependence at short wavelengths but is not its main origin. Residual offsets in absolute scale length indicate the remaining differences between simulated and observed galaxy structure.

AI.tldr: Using the TNG50-SKIRT Atlas, the paper measures wavelength-dependent disc scale lengths and shows that simulated galaxies reproduce observed scaling relations but are systematically larger, with stellar population (age) gradients as the primary driver of the wavelength dependence.
AI.motivation: To test whether simulated galaxies reproduce the structural properties and scaling relations (notably the wavelength dependence of disc scale lengths) observed in real galaxies, and to identify the physical origin of this wavelength dependence.
AI.method: Measures disc scale lengths from 1D radial surface-brightness profiles of multi-wavelength synthetic images from the TNG50-SKIRT Atlas, using an interactively defined disc-dominated region applied consistently across bands. Restricts to nearly face-on, star-forming galaxies with exponential r-band profiles. Compares dust-attenuated, dust-free images and intrinsic stellar population maps, and benchmarks against observational samples.
AI.result: Most TSA galaxies show exponential discs in mock observations and reproduce the observed scale length–mass (luminosity) relation, though they are systematically larger at fixed mass/luminosity. Scale length depends only weakly on morphology, correlates strongly across wavelengths, and decreases systematically with increasing wavelength; normalised scale lengths show a monotonic trend consistent with observations from optical to NIR. Stellar population gradients—dominated by radial age gradients, with metallicity secondary—are the primary driver, while dust attenuation enhances the short-wavelength dependence but is not its main origin.
AI.conclusion: TNG50 reproduces the qualitative wavelength dependence and scaling relations of disc scale lengths, with stellar age gradients as the dominant cause. Residual offsets in absolute scale length point to remaining structural differences between simulated and observed galaxies.

title: GAMA-23 deep field with uGMRT Band-2: source catalogue and source count
comment: 13 pages, 8 figures, 4 tables, accepted in Journal of Astrophysics and Astronomy
summary: We present the low-frequency GAMA-23 field of the Galaxy and Mass Assembly (GAMA) survey with upgraded Giant Meterwave Radio Telescope (uGMRT) observations in Band-2 ($120-250$ MHz). The on-source observation was conducted for ${\sim}5$ hours. The final image achieved an off-source RMS noise of 320 $μ$Jy beam$^{-1}$, covering an area of $5.86\,\text{deg}^2$ with restoring beam size of $15.4''{\times}8.2''$ at the central frequency of 183 MHz. The catalogue derived from the radio image includes 569 sources with a flux density limit of ${\geq}\,5σ$. The flux density measurements and the positional accuracy are cross-verified and compared with other radio catalogues available in the literature. The spectral indices derived from fitting a power law are -0.68$^{+0.18}_{-0.23}$ for the ASKAP EMU catalogue and -0.72$^{+0.19}_{-0.24}$ for the NVSS catalogue. The normalised source count derived from this catalogue is consistent with models and observations with a nominal catalogue threshold of 1.7 mJy, while the sensitivity varies across the image.

AI.tldr: The GAMA-23 field is observed with uGMRT Band-2 (120–250 MHz) for ~5 hours, yielding a 320 μJy beam⁻¹ RMS image and a 569-source catalogue at 183 MHz; flux/positional accuracy are validated cross-catalogue and the source counts agree with models.
AI.motivation: Low-frequency radio observations of well-studied extragalactic fields like GAMA-23 are needed to characterize source populations, spectral indices, and source counts, complementing higher-frequency catalogues such as ASKAP EMU and NVSS.
AI.method: uGMRT Band-2 (120–250 MHz) observation of the GAMA-23 field with ~5 h on-source integration; imaging achieved 320 μJy beam⁻¹ off-source RMS over 5.86 deg² with a 15.4''×8.2'' restoring beam at 183 MHz. A 5σ source catalogue was extracted, cross-verified against literature radio catalogues, with power-law spectral indices and normalized differential source counts derived.
AI.result: Final image reaches 320 μJy beam⁻¹ RMS over 5.86 deg² with 15.4''×8.2'' beam at 183 MHz. Catalogue contains 569 sources at ≥5σ. Spectral indices are −0.68(+0.18/−0.23) versus ASKAP EMU and −0.72(+0.19/−0.24) versus NVSS. Normalized source counts are consistent with models and observations at a nominal 1.7 mJy threshold, though sensitivity varies across the field.
AI.conclusion: The uGMRT Band-2 GAMA-23 catalogue is a reliable low-frequency dataset with validated flux and astrometric accuracy, consistent spectral indices across catalogues, and source counts matching models; it provides a valuable low-frequency reference for the GAMA field.

title: Does Topology-Dependent Chemistry Influence the Interstellar PAH Inventory? Insights from the Absence of Cyanotriphenylenes
comment: Accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal
summary: Although a set of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) has recently been identified in the cold dark cloud TMC-1, several common PAH motifs remain absent, leaving the origin of this apparent structural selectivity unresolved. Triphenylene (\ce{C18H12}) provides a stringent test of whether relative thermodynamic stability alone can account for the emerging PAH inventory because it is the smallest fully benzenoid PAH predicted by Clar's rule, is exceptionally stable, and is a key subunit of larger detected aromatic frameworks such as coronene and fullerene-related species. To probe whether such thermodynamically favored carbon skeletons are selected under cold interstellar conditions, we synthesized cyanotriphenylenes and measured their first 6.5--16~GHz microwave rotational spectra as polar tracers for the non-polar parent. An astronomical search based on these spectroscopic parameters yielded no detection, suggesting a possible ``missing triphenylene'' anomaly: despite its exceptional thermodynamic stability, this fully benzenoid PAH may be relatively depleted in TMC-1. To rationalize this behavior, we introduce a ring-node graphic representation that classifies PAH skeletons by topology; within this framework, triphenylene, whose compactness is otherwise ambiguous, is classified as non-compact. This representation reveals a tentative clustering of the currently detected and undetected PAHs according to topology, suggesting that the current PAH inventory cannot be rationalized solely on the basis of thermodynamic stability and may instead reflect differences in formation and destruction kinetics. The observed selectivity may arise from two complementary effects: sequential growth decay along bottom-up growth pathways and rapid consumption of bay-region intermediates by reactive unsaturated small species.

AI.tldr: Cyanotriphenylene rotational spectra were measured and used to search for triphenylene in TMC-1; no detection suggests a "missing triphenylene" anomaly, and a ring-node topological classification is proposed to explain PAH selectivity via kinetics rather than thermodynamic stability alone.
AI.motivation: Several common PAH motifs, including the exceptionally stable, fully benzenoid triphenylene, remain absent from the TMC-1 PAH inventory. The origin of this structural selectivity—and whether relative thermodynamic stability alone can account for it—is unresolved.
AI.method: Synthesized cyanotriphenylenes as polar proxies for non-polar triphenylene and measured their first 6.5–16 GHz microwave rotational spectra. Used the derived spectroscopic parameters to conduct an astronomical search toward TMC-1. Introduced a ring-node graphic representation to classify PAH skeletons by topology (classifying triphenylene as non-compact).
AI.result: The astronomical search yielded no detection of triphenylene, indicating a possible "missing triphenylene" anomaly. The ring-node framework shows a tentative clustering of detected versus undetected PAHs by topology.
AI.conclusion: The current PAH inventory cannot be rationalized solely by thermodynamic stability; it likely reflects differences in formation and destruction kinetics. The observed selectivity may arise from sequential growth decay along bottom-up pathways and rapid consumption of bay-region intermediates by reactive unsaturated small species.

title: A detailed star formation history of the distant Milky Way satellite Canes Venatici I: An old dwarf spheroidal forming most of its stars after reionisation
summary: Canes Venatici I (CVnI) is a distant Milky Way (MW) dwarf spheroidal (dSph) satellite. To date, there is no consensus on its evolution and the properties of its stellar population. This work is aimed at obtaining an accurate picture of the star formation history (SFH) and metallicity distribution of CVnI to reconstruct its evolution in detail, as well as to infer the possible effects of internal and external feedback. We used archival HST/ACS observations to obtain the deepest colour-magnitude diagram (CMD) to date, reaching $\sim$2 mag below the old main sequence turn-off. We derived the SFH and metallicity distribution of CVnI using a state-of-the-art CMD-fitting technique. We found that the SFH is dominated by a single star formation period, which peaked around 11.8 Gyr ago, well after the reionisation epoch, and remained active until $\sim$10.4 Gyr ago. The galaxy's global metallicity, [Z/H], ranges from -2.4 to -1.5 dex. Interestingly, while its star population is old and metal-poor, compared to other MW satellites of a similar size and luminosity that formed most of their stars in a single burst, CVnI experienced a delayed star formation period. We carried out an exhaustive set of tests with synthetic and real populations to ensure the reliability of these results. We suggest that the evolution of CVnI could have been regulated by its mass accretion history. The galaxy would have evolved above (but still close to) a theoretic redshift-dependent critical mass above which it is possible to maintain star formation. The combined effect of SN feedback would have made CVnI's halo mass subcritical at z$\approx$2, definitively quenching its star formation. We cannot rule out the possible influence of gravitational interaction of CVnI with the MW at early ages, as hinted at by the most recent calculations of its orbit.

AI.tldr: The deepest HST/ACS CMD of the Milky Way dSph Canes Venatici I reveals a single, delayed star formation episode peaking at ~11.8 Gyr ago and lasting to ~10.4 Gyr, with [Z/H] between -2.4 and -1.5 dex; the evolution is interpreted as being regulated by mass accretion history and SN feedback quenching star formation at z≈2.
AI.motivation: There is currently no consensus on the evolution of the distant MW dSph Canes Venatici I or on the properties of its stellar population; the authors aim to obtain an accurate star formation history (SFH) and metallicity distribution to reconstruct its evolution in detail and to infer the effects of internal and external feedback.
AI.method: Archival HST/ACS photometry is used to construct the deepest CMD to date, reaching ~2 mag below the old main-sequence turn-off. The SFH and metallicity distribution are derived with a state-of-the-art CMD-fitting technique, and an exhaustive set of tests with synthetic and real stellar populations is performed to validate the results.
AI.result: Star formation is dominated by a single period peaking at ~11.8 Gyr ago, well after the reionisation epoch, and continuing until ~10.4 Gyr ago. The global metallicity spans [Z/H] = -2.4 to -1.5 dex. Although old and metal-poor, CVnI shows a delayed star formation period relative to other MW satellites of similar size and luminosity that formed most of their stars in a single burst.
AI.conclusion: The authors suggest that CVnI's evolution was regulated by its mass accretion history: the galaxy evolved above (but close to) a redshift-dependent critical mass for sustaining star formation, and combined SN feedback drove its halo mass subcritical at z≈2, definitively quenching star formation. An early gravitational interaction with the MW cannot be ruled out, as hinted at by recent orbit calculations.

title: Black Hole Mass Estimation of a Background Quasar in the Vicinity of the cD Galaxy Holm 15A
summary: This study analyzes spectra from the central region of the galaxy cluster Abell 85 observed with GTC/OSIRIS, focusing on the cD galaxy Holm 15A and the point-like X-ray source SDSS J004150.75-091824.3, projected $13.74\arcsec$ from Holm 15A. For the latter, we found it is a background quasar with a redshift of $1.56386 \pm 0.00397$, ruling out the possibility of it being a rogue BH gravitationally bound to Holm 15A. In addition, using single-epoch spectroscopy, we report that the quasar J004150 hosts a Supermassive Black Hole (SMBH) with a mass of $\log(M_{\text{BH}}/\mathrm{M_{\odot}}) = 8.72 \pm 0.26$.

AI.tldr: GTC/OSIRIS spectroscopy shows the point-like X-ray source near the cD galaxy Holm 15A in Abell 85 is a background quasar at z=1.564, not a bound rogue black hole; its SMBH mass is log(M/M_sun)=8.72±0.26.
AI.motivation: The X-ray source SDSS J004150.75-091824.3 lies only 13.74″ from Holm 15A, raising the question of whether it is a rogue black hole gravitationally bound to the cD galaxy or an unrelated background object.
AI.method: Analysis of GTC/OSIRIS spectra of the central region of Abell 85, covering Holm 15A and the point-like X-ray source; redshift determination and single-epoch (virial) SMBH mass estimation for the source.
AI.result: The source is a background quasar at z=1.56386±0.00397, excluding a bound rogue-BH interpretation; its SMBH mass is log(M_BH/M_sun)=8.72±0.26.
AI.conclusion: J004150 is a background quasar rather than a rogue BH associated with Holm 15A, so it cannot be used as evidence for a recoiling/bound wandering BH in Abell 85; its own SMBH is of moderate mass.

title: UV spectra of little red dots: Broad-line N/C, gas recycling and black hole masses
comment: 11 pages, 10 figures. Comments are welcome
summary: Radiative-transfer models of supermassive black holes accreting inside dense gas cocoons reproduce the X-ray-to-near-infrared spectral energy distribution of "little red dots" (LRDs) using the code Sirocco. In the ultraviolet, these models also predict weak broad emission lines and a series of metal absorption lines, which deep spectroscopy from the JWST SPURS survey now detects in several LRDs. Here we use the models to interpret these features. We find that N and C ions of equal charge (3+ or 2+) occupy largely the same gas in the simulations, such that the combination of the broad N IV]/C IV and N III]/C III] flux ratios simultaneously constrains both the electron density and the N/C abundance ratio of the gas in the LRD proper. The nitrogen and carbon emission of SPURS-GN-2, an LRD at $z=7.19$, requires an order of magnitude nitrogen excess compared to the solar value, N/C $= 12^{+3}_{-2}$ (N/C)$_\odot$, in the broad-line gas with electron density $\log n_e = 9.7^{+0.3}_{-0.5}$ cm$^{-3}$. Thus, around half the broad-line CNO nuclei have passed through hydrogen burning. Because the ionised gas is replaced on a century timescale, sustaining this enrichment favours gas recycling. UV absorption lines test this independently. In two of the four LRDs, line blueshift velocities clearly increase with the photon energy required to ionise the absorber gas. In the models the absorption lines are spatially stratified, indicating that the gas is launched near the escape speed and slowed by gravity. In GN-2, where the measurement can be made, the inferred deceleration requires radiation pressure close to the Eddington limit of a $10^{6-7}$ M$_\odot$ black hole. The lines are also typically strongly saturated, making inferences of direct abundance ratios misleading.

AI.tldr: Sirocco radiative-transfer models of black holes accreting in dense gas cocoons interpret JWST SPURS UV features in "little red dots": broad N IV]/C IV and N III]/C III] ratios jointly fix electron density and N/C, and blueshift-stratified absorption lines indicate high-speed, gravity-decelerated outflows near the Eddington limit.
AI.motivation: Cocoon-accretion radiative-transfer models successfully reproduce the X-ray-to-NIR SED of little red dots (LRDs), and they additionally predict weak broad emission lines and metal absorption lines in the UV. JWST SPURS deep spectroscopy now detects these features in several LRDs, motivating a model-based interpretation of the emission and absorption diagnostics.
AI.method: Apply the Sirocco radiative-transfer simulations to the SPURS UV spectra. Use the joint constraint from broad N IV]/C IV and N III]/C III] flux ratios, exploiting the co-spatiality of equal-charge N and C ions (3+ or 2+) in the models, to simultaneously infer electron density and N/C abundance. Independently, analyze UV absorption-line blueshifts as a function of ionization photon energy, and model their spatial stratification, saturation, and kinematics.
AI.result: For SPURS-GN-2 (z=7.19), the broad-line gas requires an order-of-magnitude nitrogen excess, N/C = 12^{+3}_{-2} (N/C)_sun, with log n_e = 9.7^{+0.3}_{-0.5} cm^-3; roughly half of the broad-line CNO nuclei have undergone hydrogen burning. Since the ionized gas is replaced on ~century timescales, sustaining this enrichment favors gas recycling. Absorption lines in two of four LRDs show blueshift velocities increasing with ionization photon energy; models attribute this to spatial stratification of gas launched near escape speed and slowed by gravity. In GN-2, the required deceleration implies radiation pressure near the Eddington limit for a 10^6-7 M_sun black hole. Lines are typically strongly saturated, so direct abundance inferences from absorption are misleading.
AI.conclusion: Sirocco models consistently explain both the UV emission and absorption features of LRDs. Broad-line N/C and density diagnostics reveal substantial nitrogen enrichment linked to hydrogen burning and gas recycling, while stratified, saturated absorption lines trace near-Eddington, gravity-decelerated outflows; absorption-based abundance estimates should be treated with caution.

title: Beyond just a torus? Re-contextualising the AGN type paradigm using data-driven host galaxy quenching histories
comment: 14 pages, 9 figures, 1 table in main text. Accepted for publication in MNRAS
summary: The orientation of a dusty torus within a unified model explains the presence (Type-1) or absence (Type-2) of broad emission lines in Active Galactic Nuclei (AGN) spectra. This orientation-based unified model, however, fails to explain differences in host galaxy properties, such as star formation rates, of Type-1 and Type-2 AGNs. Star-formation histories (SFHs) can shed light on the connection between AGN type and host galaxy properties, but are challenging to extract from Type-1 AGN that outshine their host galaxies. We use mean-field independent component analysis (MFICA) spectrum decomposition to extract the stellar populations of $\sim$3000 optically selected Type-1 and Type-2 AGN host galaxies from the seventh data release (DR7) of the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS), matched in redshift ($0.16 \leq z \leq 0.4$) and AGN luminosity ($6.5<\log_{10} [L_{[OIII]}/L_\odot] <9.5$). Using MFICA, we find that only $\sim$10 per cent of AGN host galaxies have recently ($\lesssim1$\,Gyr) and rapidly quenched star formation following a starburst, with Type-2 AGN host galaxies having done so at most 100\,Myrs more recently than Type-1 AGN host galaxies. For most ($\sim$90 per cent) AGN hosts with normal recent star formation histories, Type-2 AGNs are associated with slightly younger stellar populations than Type-1 AGNs. The younger stellar populations of Type-2 AGN hosts can be explained by a link between dusty torus covering factors and stellar populations, by host-galaxy obscuration of AGN, or by an evolution in AGN type without major bursts or rapid quenching of star formation.

AI.tldr: Using MFICA spectral decomposition on ~3000 matched SDSS Type-1 and Type-2 AGN hosts, the authors find that only ~10% have recently and rapidly quenched post-starburst star formation, and that Type-2 hosts overall host slightly younger stellar populations than Type-1 hosts.
AI.motivation: The orientation-based unified model explains the presence/absence of broad emission lines (Type-1 vs Type-2) but cannot account for reported differences in host-galaxy properties such as star formation rates. Star-formation histories could link AGN type to host properties, but extracting them from Type-1 AGN, whose bright nuclei outshine the host, is difficult.
AI.method: Mean-field independent component analysis (MFICA) spectrum decomposition applied to ~3000 optically selected Type-1 and Type-2 AGN host galaxies from SDSS DR7, matched in redshift (0.16 ≤ z ≤ 0.4) and AGN luminosity (6.5 < log10[L_[OIII]/L_sun] < 9.5), to isolate and characterize the stellar populations of the hosts.
AI.result: Only ~10% of AGN hosts show recent (≲1 Gyr) rapid quenching of star formation following a starburst, with Type-2 hosts having quenched at most ~100 Myr more recently than Type-1 hosts. For the majority (~90%) with normal recent star-formation histories, Type-2 AGNs are associated with slightly younger stellar populations than Type-1 AGNs.
AI.conclusion: The younger stellar populations in Type-2 hosts may be explained by a link between dusty torus covering factors and stellar populations, by host-galaxy obscuration of the AGN, or by an evolution in AGN type without major starbursts or rapid star-formation quenching.
